topic: Field decay >=28 nT/year — deep-attack review of EXP-596 rewrite (6 patches, ISS-2618)

holes_found.description: CARRY-OVER (c5 holes_found[1], not yet routed to an ISS): the self-undercutting long-run-rate sentence survived the EXP-596 rewrite untouched. detail_evidence still supports 'the 28 nT/yr threshold is met at SAA-core stations on the long-run rate' with the parenthetical '(the dome's own regional confirmation cites ~30 nT over 14 months)' which the same sentence then annualizes to 25.7 < 28 — in-line evidence undercutting the claim it supports. Timing explains the miss: EXP-596 was authored 2026-06-06T23:17, BEFORE c5 was written (2026-06-07T00:12), so the rewrite could not have incorporated c5's finding; EXP-596's own summary says the 25.7 cross-reference was left 'untouched per c4 guidance'. The fix material now sits one paragraph away in the same field: the dome's station-table rows (TSU -77, Keetmanshoop -76 — multi-station, 2.7-2.8x the threshold) are exactly the long-run support c5's rewrite spec called for.
holes_found.recommendation: Micro-patch (small blast radius now that the rewrite landed): replace the parenthetical with the table-derived support, e.g. 'the 28 nT/yr threshold is met at SAA-region stations on the long-run rate (the dome's own table cites -77 and -76 nT/yr at its Namibian stations)', and move the ~30 nT/14-month -> 25.7 nT/yr arithmetic into its own sentence attacking WIN-037's confirmation window specifically. Decider: no open ISS exists for this carry-over — create one.

holes_found.description: Suppressed exculpatory context on the TSU/TTB two-continent attack. monitor.py line 489's own comment reads 'SAA Decay Rate (Tsumeb TTB)' — the dome author conflates the Namibian station name and the Brazilian IAGA code in a single breath, making 'miscoded station label' the most natural reading. Our published text presents only the maximal contrast ('TTB is Tatuoca, Brazil, ~7,800 km away on another continent') and omits the comment, even though EXP-596's own verification_performed quotes it — our audit trail proves we had it in hand. A defender who opens monitor.py sees the comment immediately and can accuse us of manufacturing a two-continent scandal from an obvious typo while suppressing the line that shows it.
holes_found.recommendation: Quote the comment and recast: the dome's own code comment conflates the two stations ('Tsumeb TTB'); whichever observatory the 77.0 actually belongs to, the page and the code disagree on the source label AND the value is hardcoded either way. This is both more honest and strictly stronger — the conflation is now a verbatim dome-side error, not our inference. Coordinate with open ISS-2605 (same Tsumeb/TTB naming issue in WIN-037) so both WINs get the same framing.

holes_found.description: Overbroad in-line support: detail_evidence asserts the -32 row 'matches no published field model' but the only in-line citation is IGRF-12 (Thebault et al. 2015) — a model generation two releases old, while the dome's stated window is 2024-2025 (IGRF-13 2019, IGRF-14 2024, plus CHAOS-7/WMM2025-era secular variation all exist). The conclusion survives — no current-generation model puts global-average decline anywhere near 32 nT/yr — but the claim quantifies over ALL published models while citing one dated one. Defender opening: 'they bound 2024-2025 decay with a 2015 model; decay has accelerated since.'
holes_found.recommendation: Either add a current-generation citation (IGRF-14/WMM2025-era global secular variation) next to the Thebault reference, or narrow the phrase to 'is 1.5-2x the IGRF global decline'. Small edit; can ride along with the holes_found[0] micro-patch.

holes_found.description: Distance overstated: detail_evidence says TTB is '~7,800 km away' from Tsumeb. Great-circle TSU (19.20S, 17.58E) to TTB (1.20S, 48.51W) computes to ~7,460 km (verified this run). ~5% high, on a number we introduced while attacking the dome for unsourced figures.
holes_found.recommendation: Change '~7,800 km' to '~7,500 km' (or 'more than 7,000 km'). Fold into the holes_found[1] rewording.

stronger_arguments.description: Same-day registration binds the duplicates together on the dome's own page: PROS-007 (-> WIN-037) and PRED-012 (-> WIN-042) were BOTH 'Registered 2026-03-06', and PROS-007's own prediction text reads 'consistent with the accelerating decay rate trajectory toward PRED-012's 2030 target' — the dome's page itself describes the two as one trajectory, registered in one batch, confirmed against the same INTERMAGNET/WMM2025 data. This converts our 'mathematically equivalent' argument into 'the dome's own registration record treats them as one claim'.

stronger_arguments.description: Threshold-provenance concession: PROS-007 states 'The 28 nT threshold was derived from the INTERMAGNET 2000-2025 trend line.' The dome's own page concedes the validation threshold comes from the very dataset used to confirm it — predicting that a trend line continues, then confirming the threshold against the same data, is circular. This is dome-side verbatim support for our derives_from_dome=false tag and for WIN-041's existing circularity argument ('a threshold the model itself defined').

The WIN-042 'Dome vs Globe' row strawmans mainstream geomagnetism: 'Globe predicts gradual linear decay toward reversal over ~1,500 years.' Standard geophysics makes no scheduled-reversal prediction and does not model secular variation as linear; and the dome's counter-assertion 'Exponential, not linear, is what the data shows' is offered with no fit statistics for either functional form. Currently our text doesn't touch this row; a one-sentence addition would close it.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome is pointing at real, fast SAA-region decay: its Namibian rows (Tsumeb -77, Keetmanshoop -76 nT/yr — wins.html WIN-042 table, retrieved this run) are the right order of magnitude for the fastest-declining region of the present secular-variation field, consistent with the dome's own WIN-041 station set (TDC -79.7 to KOU -31.0, same page). And the dome genuinely did register PRED-012 (2026-03-06) before declaring confirmation (2026-03-21) — a real, if self-hosted and self-graded, registration step (wins.html WIN-042 block).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: The prediction is GLOBAL ('Global geomagnetic field decay >=28 nT/year by 2030', wins.html WIN-042 'Prediction' row): regional extremes don't satisfy it, and the only global figure offered (-32) is unsourced and 1.5-2x the IGRF-12 global decline (doi:10.1186/s40623-015-0228-9; ratios 32/21=1.52, 32/15=2.13 verified this run). The confirming data ('INTERMAGNET observatories, 2024-2025') predates the registration, and the same measurement is already banked as WIN-037 — registered the same day, per the dome's own PROS-007 block (wins.json:WIN-042.tldr_verdict; wins.html PROS-007).
